status_summary: HRSA's FY 2026 General Terms and Conditions, applying to awards made on or after 2026-03-11, add a section requiring funded activities to align with HRSA priorities, including not supporting medical interventions for gender dysphoria in minors that lack a strong evidence base and applying sex-based definitions grounded in biology. Ryan White notices of funding opportunity carry restrictive terms: HRSA-26-074 (Part B supplemental, application deadline 2026-07-10) bars funds for denial by the recipient of the sex binary and carries the gender dysphoria and sex-based definition priorities, and HRSA-26-012 (ADAP Emergency Relief Funds) limits sex hormones dispensed by an AIDS Drug Assistance Program to treating HIV/AIDS. The government's court filing says such notices were first published 2026-06-04 and plaintiffs give 2026-06-08, but HRSA-26-012 states an issue date of 2025-10-02, so the date of the first restrictive notice is unreconciled. These restrictive terms are operative. Provider groups challenged the general terms and the notice terms in the District of Massachusetts on 2026-06-10 (No. 1:26-cv-12638-WGY); a bench trial was held 2026-09-23, a joint notice of 2026-10-02 told the court it need not withhold adjudication further, the government filed a post-hearing brief on 2026-10-09, and no ruling was found as of 2026-10-26. No withdrawal of the 2021 guidance was found: the HRSA HIV/AIDS Bureau letter of 2021-12-16 stating that Ryan White funds may be used to support gender affirming care remained posted on hab.hrsa.gov on 2026-10-26 with no rescission notice, the Ryan White policy notices page marks no notice rescinded or withdrawn, and no source read states that earlier HRSA guidance on gender transition services was withdrawn.

title: Withdraw HRSA Ryan White guidance allowing funds for gender transition support
uncertainties: The HRSA FY 2026 General Terms and Conditions and the government's 2026-10-09 post-hearing brief were read. Two Ryan White notices of funding opportunity were read on grants.gov on 2026-10-26: HRSA-26-074 (Part B States/Territories Supplemental, application deadline 2026-07-10, no issue date found in the part read) bars funds for denial of the sex binary (p. 3) and carries the gender dysphoria and sex-based definition priorities (p. 40), and HRSA-26-012 (ADAP Emergency Relief Funds) limits sex hormones dispensed by an ADAP to treating HIV/AIDS (p. 41). HRSA-26-012 states an issue date of 2025-10-02, earlier than the 2026-06-04 date the government gives for the first notice and the 2026-06-08 date plaintiffs' counsel gives; whether the file was revised after issue is not shown, so the date of the first restrictive notice is unreconciled. The HRSA HIV/AIDS Bureau letter of 2021-12-16 stating that Ryan White funds may be used to support gender affirming care remained posted on hab.hrsa.gov on 2026-10-26 with no rescission or withdrawal notice. The HRSA Ryan White policy notices page (last reviewed January 2026) was read in review: no notice is marked rescinded or withdrawn, no notice title concerns gender transition services, and the page carries a general disclaimer about content promoting gender ideology without naming any notice; neither the brief nor the terms state that earlier guidance was withdrawn, so withdrawal remains unverified. A joint exhibit list of 2026-09-01 names an HRSA Administrator letter to Ryan White awardees dated 2026-04-07 (Ex. 28), which was not opened. The Georgetown tracker docket page lists entries through 2026-10-09 (including a motion to dismiss of 2026-08-14 and an untitled order of 2026-09-11) and no ruling, but labels the case stayed without explanation; a news report of 2026-09-26 describes the 2026-09-23 bench trial, says no ruling issued from the bench and that the judge agreed to defer a decision until after 2026-10-02 while settlement was considered. A joint notice of 2026-10-02 (Document 85, No. 1:26-cv-12638-WGY, read on the Georgetown tracker) tells the court it need not withhold adjudication any further, which (inference) indicates the settlement talks ended and the case awaits decision. The court docket itself was not opened (courtlistener.com refuses automated fetches; the clearinghouse.net case page failed to load), and no ruling was found as of 2026-10-26. The match is partial because the recommendation asks for withdrawal of guidance while the action restricts funding through award terms.
